# S243 — Claude fallback implementer: shell rules in the brief, a short denied count in status

When the Claude implementer (matrix row r3) stands in for Codex, ork gives it two fixes. (a) Its brief says which shell commands it may use and how (Claude only). (c) `ork status` shows a short count of denied commands instead of their text. Part (b), one automatic nudge on a report shape pause, was dropped on 2026-11-04 because S275 landed that retry; the letters (a) and (c) are kept so earlier notes and decisions still match.

**Findings:**  · **Size:** M · **Tree:**

**2026-11-04** — Owner 2026-11-04 (ork S287 Q2): part (b) dropped because S275 landed the automatic same-session retry; parts (a) and (c) stay.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:**

## Why

Wave 5 (2026-11-02, owner's report of S238 and S190, which ork ran): Codex was out of credits at launch, ork fell back to the Claude implementer (matrix row r3, claude sonnet high), and both runs paused with `report shape: no "Tests: N passed, M failed" line; no "## Owner needed" section; next: ork retry RUN`. The status line then printed the denied Bash commands. The owner decided on 2026-11-02 (interactive) that this goes in pass v1.1 and chose three parts, called option (3): (a) shell rules for the Claude implementer, (b) one automatic nudge on a report shape pause, (c) a short denied count in status. Whether ork should hold an engine-slice run until Codex's out-until time instead of falling back to Claude is not decided and is not part of this slice.

Owner 2026-11-04 (ork S287 Q2, "drop-part-b", accepted): part (b) is out of this slice. S275 (landed on main as 9865f1e) already retries a shape-only report error once, in the same round and session, for the implementer (and its finish step), reviewer, gate, architect and UI pass (`runRound`, `internal/engine/round.go:532-551`, `AutomaticShapeRetry`; `docs/design.md:575-588`). A second retry path beside it would duplicate that. This slice is now parts (a) and (c).

What the code at HEAD of main shows (verified 2026-11-02; re-verified 2026-11-04 at b9b905c, line numbers updated):

- The Claude implementer runs on an allowlist. `DefaultImplementerAllowlist` (`internal/engine/perm.go:24-36`) holds `Read`, `Grep`, `Glob`, `Edit`, `Write` and prefix patterns such as `Bash(slicer *)`, `Bash(go -C * test*)`, `Bash(gofmt *)`, plus `Bash(<check command>*)`. It has no `sed`, `python3`, `cd`, `grep` or `rg` entry. A registry `permissions.implementer` list replaces the default as is (`ResolvePermission`, `perm.go:47-71`; `TestImplementerGetsTheRegistryAllowlistAsIs`, `perm_test.go:36`). The Claude adapter passes the list as `--allowedTools a,b --permission-prompts none` (`internal/agent/claude/args.go:48-60`), and Codex gets `workspace-write` or `read-only` instead (`internal/agent/codex/codex.go:53-56`). So a `sed -i`, a `python3` heredoc or a `cd X && ...` command matches no default pattern, and it is denied for Claude and runs for Codex.
- The brief does not list the allowlist. `BriefInput` (`internal/engine/brief.go:20-38`) has no allowlist field, and `runRound` builds it at `internal/engine/round.go:283-292` without `perm.Allow` (`perm` is resolved at `round.go:239` and its `Allow` goes only to the runner request, `round.go:366`). `ork run` prints the allowlist (`internal/cli/run.go:200`), but the role never sees it.
- The role prompt is one file for every vendor. `roles.Prompt(name)` takes no vendor (`internal/roles/roles.go:45-54`), and `internal/roles/prompts/implementer.md` is embedded and canonical (`roles.prompts`, adj 29). `TestNoClaudeCodeOnlyMechanics` (`internal/roles/roles_test.go:248`) forbids the word Bash in a prompt. The brief builder already branches on the vendor (`brief.go:98`, the UI pass skills line). So a Claude-only line belongs in `BuildBrief`, and `implementer.md` stays as it is (Codex unchanged).
- The status line prints at most three denials in full and then `and N more` (`source.DenialsText`, `internal/source/source.go:282-287`; used at `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:101-103`). Each denial text is `Tool: command` capped at 200 characters (`internal/agent/claude/types.go:74,82-101`; `internal/runrec/record.go:77-92`), so three Bash denials can fill several lines. The daemon builds `EngineRun.Denials` as distinct texts in first-seen order with ` xN` for repeats (`internal/daemon/runs.go:1325-1342`, field at `internal/source/source.go:274`). The TUI uses the same `DenialsText` (`internal/tui/overview.go:389,995`).

Historical, part (b) only (2026-11-02, before S275; no longer true at HEAD): a shape error paused the run at once, and `ork retry RUN` resumed the role with a `## Report shape` section. S275 replaced that with the automatic retry above.

Not verified (the run logs are outside the workspace and were not read):

- Why the two final reports lacked the shape. A report file that is missing or empty falls back to the vendor's final message text (`Engine.readReport`, `internal/engine/round.go:630-649`), which would lack both parts; that is consistent with what happened but not shown.
- Which exact commands Sonnet was denied. The five kinds the owner named (a `python3` heredoc edit, `sed -i` on a Go file, `grep` into `sed`, `cd` then `sed`, `rg` pipelines) match no default pattern, as above. Whether the ork project's registry entry holds `Bash(rg *)` is not shown in the workspace; the default list has no `rg`.
- That Claude Code's matcher refuses a pipe, `cd`, a heredoc or `sed -i` after an allowed prefix. That is Claude Code's behaviour, not ork's; the repo's fixtures show only a denied `Write` (`testdata/vendors/claude/04-allowlist-denies-write.stdout`).
- The status line printing "every" command. At HEAD it prints at most three, each up to 200 characters, then a count.

Design choices (*proposed* until an adj record decides them):

- The shell rules are a section of the Claude implementer's brief, built from the allowlist the role really has, not text in the shared prompt.
- `ork status` counts distinct denial texts and shows the first one cut to 40 characters. `--json` and the TUI are unchanged.
- (Dropped 2026-11-04 with part (b): the nudge's scope, its not-a-round rule and its budget rule. S275 settled those for its own retry.)

Owner decisions (interactive question, 2026-11-02): the three parts were the whole slice (part (b) since dropped, above); the answers stated in this spec are accepted as written (the denied count reads as stated; the nudge answers no longer apply); the spec check keeps its own existing retry; ork keeps falling back to the Claude implementer when Codex is out (it does not hold the run). Related owner rule, 2026-11-02: for Grok and any other vendor, do not pin a model version unless the owner asks; default to the vendor's latest.

## Failing tests

Part (a), `internal/engine/brief_test.go`:

- TestClaudeImplementerBriefHasShellRules: `BriefInput{Role: RoleImplementer, Vendor: "claude", Allowlist: DefaultImplementerAllowlist("go test ./...")}`. The brief has a `## Shell commands` section that says to change files with the Edit and Write tools, to run one plain command per shell call, and not to use pipes, `cd`, heredocs, scripts or `sed -i`. It lists every `Bash(...)` entry of the allowlist as the pattern inside the parentheses (`slicer *`, `go -C * test*`, `go test ./...*`) and the other entries as tool names. Fails first: it does not compile, because `BriefInput` has no `Allowlist` field; after the field exists, it fails because there is no section.
- TestShellRulesOnlyForTheClaudeImplementer: no `## Shell commands` section, and a brief equal to the one built without `Allowlist`, for a codex implementer, an empty vendor, `Claude` (case-sensitive), and a claude reviewer, gate, architect, UI pass and spec-check. Fails first: compile error as above (no `Allowlist` field).
- TestShellSectionFollowsTheRegistryAllowlist: a list of `Edit` and `Bash(dotnet test*)` shows `dotnet test*` and `Edit` and none of the default entries (`slicer *` is absent). A list with no `Bash(` entry says the role has no shell commands. A check command with a backtick or newline in its entry stays inside a fence that is longer than any backtick run in it (the rule of `fenceFor`, `brief.go:40-52`). Fails first: no section.
- TestFinishStepBriefKeepsTheShellSection: with `Finish: true` the section is still present (the finish step runs `slicer` commands). Fails first: no section.

Part (a), `internal/engine/fallback_test.go` or `internal/engine/brief_test.go` (use `fallbackHarness` at `fallback_test.go:81`):

- TestClaudeFallbackBriefListsTheRealAllowlist: codex row exits `ExitOutOfCredits`, the claude row runs. The claude request's brief has `## Shell commands` and every `Bash(...)` pattern of that request's `Allowlist`; the codex request's brief has no such section. Fails first: the section is missing.

Part (c), `internal/cli`:

- TestStatusCountsDeniedCommands: five denials, the first a 120-character `Bash: ...` text. `ork status` prints `(denied: 5 commands, first: ` plus the first text cut to 40 characters ending in `...`, then `)`; none of the other four texts appears; the line has no text beyond the cut. Fails first: it prints `A, B, C and 2 more` style text.
- TestStatusDeniedOneCommandIsSingular: one denial of 12 characters prints `(denied: 1 command, first: Write: /x.txt)` with no cut. Fails first: old format.
- TestStatusDeniedCutsOnRunesNotBytes: a first denial with multi-byte characters is cut on a rune boundary (valid UTF-8). Fails first: old format.
- TestStatusJSONKeepsEveryDenial: `ork status --json` prints the daemon's `denials` array exactly as received (five long texts). Fails first: passes today; keep it as a guard for "the data in --json is unchanged".

## Implement

Tests first. Watch each fail for the stated reason before the product code.

Do not touch: `internal/roles/prompts/implementer.md` and every other prompt, `internal/source/source.go` (`DenialsText` stays for the TUI), `internal/tui` and `testdata/golden`, `internal/daemon/runs.go` (the `denials` data and `--json` stay as they are), `internal/engine/speccheck.go`, `internal/engine/perm.go`, and S275's shape retry in `round.go` (`AutomaticShapeRetry`).

1. Part (a), tests: write the four brief tests and the fallback test. Add the field and the section last.
2. Part (a), product: add `Allowlist []string` to `BriefInput`. In `BuildBrief`, after the "Checks ork runs" block and before the round's own sections, when `in.Role == RoleImplementer && in.Vendor == "claude"` (case-sensitive, as `brief.go:98`), write `## Shell commands`. Text (*proposed*): "ork limits your shell to the commands below. Any other command is denied and does not run. Change files with the Edit and Write tools only: no `sed -i`, no scripts (python or others), no heredocs, no redirects into files. Run one plain command per shell call: no pipes, no `&&` or `;`, no command substitution, no `cd` (use absolute paths, `go -C DIR` and `git -C DIR`). If a command is denied, use an allowed form; do not retry it another way." Then "Tools: " plus the non-Bash entries, and the `Bash(...)` entries as their inner patterns, one per line, in one fenced block (fence length by `fenceFor`, `brief.go:40-52`; a trailing `*` means any further text). An allowlist with no Bash entry says the role has no shell commands. Do not rewrite the entries. In `runRound` (`round.go:283-292`) set `Allowlist: perm.Allow`. A read-only role has no list, and the section is not written for it.
3. Part (a), docs: in `docs/design.md`, beside the S209 Skills paragraph (`:323-330`), say that a `claude` implementer's brief has a `## Shell commands` section built from its allowlist, and that the prompt stays vendor-neutral; mark it *proposed*.
4. Part (c), tests: write the three status tests and the JSON guard; update the three pinned old texts.
5. Part (c), product, in `internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:101-103`: replace `source.DenialsText(r.Denials)` with a small helper in `internal/cli` that prints `(denied: N command[s], first: TEXT)`, where N is `len(r.Denials)` (distinct texts), `TEXT` is `r.Denials[0]` cut to 40 runes (37 runes and `...` when longer). Do not change `source.DenialsText` (the TUI uses it), `EngineRun.Denials`, or `--json`.
6. Part (c), docs: `docs/dashboard.md:662-670` (a sentence: `ork status` prints the count and the first denial cut to 40 characters; `ork status --json` lists every denial; the Overview rows are as before), `docs/state.md:472-477`, and `docs/design.md:1667-1670`.
7. CHANGELOG, last, so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict: add one entry at the bottom of `## Unreleased` that starts "Claude fallback implementer:" and says: the Claude implementer's brief lists its allowed shell commands and the rules for them (*proposed*); `ork status` shows a count of denied commands and the first one cut short (*proposed*).
